title: Develop, Preview, Test: why end-to-end tests on every deploy beat the testing pyramid
summary: Guillermo Rauch argues that testing is an investment judged by return and risk, and that modern infrastructure now makes E2E tests the best return. Per-push preview deployments plus headless browsers on serverless compute make prod-like staging and fast, cheap tests possible. He demos a Vercel, Checkly and GitHub workflow set up in minutes.

principles.text: Treat writing tests as an investment: weigh return and risk, including opportunity cost versus shipping features.
principles.quote: Writing tests is an **investment**, and like any other investment, it has to be evaluated in terms of its **return** and **risks**

principles.text: Prioritize E2E tests on the critical parts of your app; they reduce risk and give the best return.
principles.quote: I want to make the case that **prioritizing end-to-end (E2E) testing** for the critical parts of your app will reduce risk and give you the best return.

principles.text: Focus on the customer first: it is the best way to run a business and to judge software quality.
principles.quote: is the best way to run a business, but also the best way to ascertain software quality.

principles.text: Quality is more than correctness: it includes reliability over time and performance.
principles.quote: (whether your program stays working correctly over time)

principles.text: Give every push its own prod-like preview URL instead of one shared staging server, so tests run against real production infrastructure.
principles.quote: Instead of thinking about a single staging server that end-to-end tests are run against, now you can have millions of concurrent "staging" environments.

principles.text: Keep testing continuously the way users experience your product to tame the chaos of complex, ever-changing dependencies.
principles.quote: continuously testing just like our users do is our best bet to tame the chaos.
